user.title: Welcome
user.description:
EyeBond Local will help you find and add a compatible device with as little manual setup as possible.

{welcome_hint}

data_description.connection_type: Choose how Home Assistant should reach the device.

collector_network.title: Collector Network Setup
collector_network.description:
Is the collector already on the same network as Home Assistant? If yes, choose the first option.

If not, two ways to get it online:
- **Bluetooth** (second option) — the easiest path on newer collectors. Needs Bluetooth on the Home Assistant side: a local adapter or an ESPHome Bluetooth Proxy near the collector.
- **The collector's own Wi-Fi** — connect the Home Assistant host to the access point the collector broadcasts (the SSID contains the collector PN, the password is usually `12345678`), then choose the first option.

After the device is added, you can move the collector onto your normal Wi-Fi from the integration settings.

manual.title: Manual Setup
manual.description:
For setups the auto-scan cannot reach: a remote collector, VPN/NAT, or a known fixed address. The settings are probed first — if the device is not confirmed, you can adjust them and retry on the next screen.

{verification_note}

data_description.server_ip: Local Home Assistant IPv4 address used to bind the EyeBond TCP listener. For normal LAN setups, choose the interface on the same subnet as the collector.
data_description.collector_ip: Collector IPv4 address to probe directly. Leave empty for local broadcast discovery. For remote or NAT setups, set the public or forwarded IPv4 that reaches the collector.
data_description.driver_hint: Auto-detect works for most inverters. Override only if instructed.
data_description.connection_strategy: Choose “Collector connects to Home Assistant on its own” if the collector already points at Home Assistant. Choose “Ask the collector to connect when needed” to have Home Assistant send a single request to the address above each time it needs data.
data_description.driver_detection_strategy: Fast mode is recommended. Use full scan when an inverter may answer through several supported protocols and you want to choose between them.

advanced_connection.name: Advanced connection settings
advanced_connection.description: Only needed for remote, VPN, or NAT setups. For a normal home network the defaults are correct — you can leave everything here untouched.

data_description.tcp_port: Local TCP listener port on Home Assistant. Default: 8899.
data_description.advertised_server_ip: Public or forwarded IP the collector should call back to. Leave empty for normal home networks (the local address above is used).
data_description.advertised_tcp_port: Forwarded external port for the callback. Leave empty unless your router forwards a different external port.
data_description.udp_port: Port used to discover the collector on the network. Default: 58899 — change only if instructed.
data_description.discovery_target: IPv4 address that receives discovery packets. Use subnet broadcast for local LAN, or a specific remote/NAT IPv4 for unicast discovery.
data_description.discovery_interval: How often to send discovery redirects while waiting for the collector.
data_description.heartbeat_interval: How often Home Assistant pings the collector to keep the connection alive.

manual_recovery_confirm.title: Verify recovery
manual_recovery_confirm.description: Step 2 of 2. Collector **{collector_pn}** was identified at **{collector_ip}**. Home Assistant will now verify that the connection can be restored when needed: it restarts the collector, waits for an autonomous reconnection, and requests a callback if necessary. Continue when you are ready.

manual_recovery_inbound_confirm.title: Collector reconnects on its own
manual_recovery_inbound_confirm.description:
Collector **{collector_pn}** proved it reconnects to Home Assistant BY ITSELF after a restart — no callback request was needed (none was sent).

Save it as an inbound collector? Home Assistant will passively wait for its connections and never send callback triggers.

error.collector_endpoint_write_failed: Could not write the Home Assistant callback endpoint to the collector.

error.already_added_candidate: This detected device is already configured and cannot be added again.
error.smartess_cloud_assist_failed: SmartESS cloud assist did not complete. See the explanation above and try again.
error.inverter_link_down: The collector responded, but the inverter link is down (identity registers read as zeros). Check the inverter power and the collector cable, then rescan.
error.callback_identity_mismatch: A different collector answered at this address. Check that the address reaches the collector you are adding, then try again.
error.callback_timeout: The collector did not call back. Check the address and that the collector can reach Home Assistant, then try again.
error.callback_trigger_not_sent: Home Assistant could not send the connection request. Another connection attempt may be in progress -- wait a moment and try again.
error.callback_identity_unverified: The collector identity could not be confirmed. Enter an address Home Assistant can reach the collector on, then try again.
error.callback_identity_ambiguous: More than one collector answered. Make sure only the collector you are adding can reach Home Assistant, then try again.
error.callback_identity_conflict: This collector is already being set up in another flow. Finish or cancel that one, then try again.
error.collector_identity_required: This collector could not be identified. Enter an address Home Assistant can reach the collector on so its identity is confirmed, then try again.
error.callback_target_required: An address is required to ask the collector to connect.
error.callback_trigger_interference: Another connection request ran at the same time, so the answer could not be attributed. Try again.

abort.collector_identity_required: This collector could not be identified. Enter an address Home Assistant can reach the collector on so its identity is confirmed, then try again.
abort.already_configured: This collector or inverter is already configured.
abort.reconfigure_entry_missing: The entry to reconfigure no longer exists.
abort.reconfigure_not_required: This entry already has a confirmed collector identity; there is nothing to repair.
abort.recovery_contract_conflict: The verified recovery proof could not be stored: the entry already carries a recovery record for a different collector or one that cannot be read. Remove or repair that entry, then try again.
abort.recovery_ownership_unavailable: The verified recovery session is no longer held for this collector. Run the verification again.
abort.background_discovery_refreshed: Background discovery is already enabled. Connected collectors were checked again.
